metadata.title: मनरेगा के गड्ढों ने जिंदगी बचाई | Life After MNREGA: Adivasi Voices from Maharashtra
metadata.description:
The Modi government has scrapped MNREGA and introduced a new law aimed at generating employment in rural India. The move has sparked a nationwide debate. Experts argue that the new law, along with the 2026 budget allocation, is insufficient to replace the scale and stability MNREGA provided.

There are growing concerns that the economic security MNREGA ensured—especially in tribal regions—may now be at risk. The main opposition party is demanding the immediate restoration of MNREGA, calling it a lifeline for rural and Adivasi communities.

Amid this debate, Main Bhi Bharat Editor Shyam Sunder travelled to Nandurbar, the poorest district of India’s richest state, Maharashtra. Through ground reporting and conversations with Adivasi families, he tries to understand what MNREGA truly meant to them—and how this law transformed Adivasi lives by providing dignity, stability, and survival-level security.

This report asks a crucial question: Can the new law really replace MNREGA on the ground?
